quests.sentence: I saw that documentary two nights ago.
quests.hint: Notice the named specific time here — weigh that against the unspecified-time option.
quests.explanation: Saw is the simple past form; a common mistake here would be using the present perfect with a specific named time.

quests.sentence: I've seen three documentaries this month.
quests.hint: 'This month' is still an open, unfinished period.
quests.explanation: Have seen is the present perfect form, correctly used because the time period named hasn't ended yet.

quests.sentence: He graduated top of his class in 2015.
quests.hint: Notice the specific year named here, regardless of how impressive the achievement is.
quests.explanation: Graduated is the simple past form, correctly used here because a specific past year anchors the event.

quests.sentence: I ate breakfast, packed my bag, and left for school.
quests.hint: These actions are told in the order they happened, so no earlier-past form is needed.
quests.explanation: Ate, packed, and left are simple past forms; using the past perfect here would be unnecessary since the sequence is already clear.

quests.sentence: I'd already left for school by the time my brother woke up.
quests.hint: This time, one event genuinely needs marking as earlier than the other past event.
quests.explanation: Had left (shortened to 'd left) is the past perfect form, correctly used because 'by the time' establishes an earlier-later relationship.

quests.sentence: She called her mom right after the flight landed.
quests.hint: 'Right after' already makes the order clear on its own.
quests.explanation: Called is the simple past form; the past perfect would be unnecessary here since the sequence is already obvious.

quests.sentence: I understand your concern completely.
quests.hint: Understanding is a mental state, so it should never appear in a progressive form like 'am understanding'.
quests.explanation: Understand is a stative verb and stays in the simple present; the progressive form would be a common mistake here.

quests.sentence: This cake tastes fantastic.
quests.hint: Here, 'taste' describes a quality, so it stays out of the progressive form.
quests.explanation: Tastes is used statively here to describe a quality, so the simple present is correct rather than a progressive form.

quests.sentence: I'm considering a few different options right now.
quests.hint: Here, 'consider' describes an active mental process, unlike a fixed state such as understanding or believing.
quests.explanation: Am considering is the present progressive form, correctly used because consider describes an ongoing process here.

quests.sentence: I've already decided — I'm taking the earlier flight.
quests.hint: This is a settled plan, so it needs a form that shows a fixed arrangement rather than a spur-of-the-moment choice.
quests.explanation: Am taking is the present progressive form, correctly used for a definite plan already decided, rather than the will-future.

quests.sentence: Watch out, that ladder is going to tip over!
quests.hint: Something visible right now is the evidence behind this warning.
quests.explanation: Is going to tip over uses going to correctly, since the prediction is based on clear present evidence.

quests.sentence: I have no idea what to order — I'll just get whatever you're having.
quests.hint: This decision is being made on the spot, not planned in advance.
quests.explanation: Will get is the will-future form, correctly used for a decision made at the moment of speaking.

quests.sentence: By the time she finished college, she had already started her own business.
quests.hint: One event needs to be marked as happening before the other past event, college finishing.
quests.explanation: Had started is the past perfect form; a common mistake would be using the present perfect here instead, which wouldn't fit a past-tense story.

quests.sentence: I have watched that movie so many times I know all the lines by heart.
quests.hint: No specific past time is mentioned, and the result is still true right now.
quests.explanation: Have watched is the present perfect form, correctly used because there's no specific past time and the result carries into the present.

quests.sentence: After the workshop ended, participants said they had learned more in two hours than in the entire semester.
quests.hint: The learning is presented as happening before the moment they made the comment.
quests.explanation: Had learned is the past perfect form, correctly placing the learning before the later past moment of speaking.

quests.sentence: I haven't seen her in ages.
quests.hint: No specific time is given, and the situation continues up to now.
quests.explanation: Haven't seen is the present perfect form, correctly used without a specific past time attached.

quests.sentence: I saw her a few years ago at a wedding.
quests.hint: This names one specific occasion, unlike the vaguer situation in the previous sentence.
quests.explanation: Saw is the simple past form, correctly used because a specific past occasion is described.

quests.sentence: This week has been incredibly stressful.
quests.hint: 'This week' hasn't finished yet.
quests.explanation: Has been is the present perfect form, correctly used because the time period referred to is still ongoing.

quests.sentence: The plane had already boarded by the time we reached the gate.
quests.hint: The boarding needs to be marked as happening before our arrival, an earlier point in the story.
quests.explanation: Had boarded is the past perfect form, correctly showing the boarding was complete before we arrived.

quests.sentence: We reached the gate two minutes after boarding began.
quests.hint: 'Two minutes after' already makes the order between these events explicit.
quests.explanation: Reached is the simple past form; the past perfect isn't needed since the order is already clear from the wording.

quests.sentence: The gate agent told us the flight was full before we could even ask about seats.
quests.hint: This is the main reported action, told as a simple sequential event.
quests.explanation: Told is the simple past form, describing the central action of this short story.

quests.sentence: I've lived in this city my whole life.
quests.hint: This describes a duration with no specific starting time named, continuing to now.
quests.explanation: Have lived is the present perfect form, correctly used for an ongoing lifelong situation.

quests.sentence: I moved here when I was five years old.
quests.hint: Notice the specific past time given by 'when I was five'.
quests.explanation: Moved is the simple past form, correctly used because a specific past time is given.

quests.sentence: This is the first time I've tried Thai food.
quests.hint: This is a standard pattern: 'the first time' pairs with a verb form that connects the experience to right now.
quests.explanation: Have tried is the present perfect form, correctly used in the common 'this is the first time...' pattern.

quests.sentence: The report looks finished, but I know for a fact she's still working on the conclusion.
quests.hint: Appearances can be misleading — trust the stated fact about what's still happening.
quests.explanation: Is working is the present progressive form, correctly describing an action still in progress despite appearances.

quests.sentence: She finished the introduction and the body sections yesterday.
quests.hint: This names a specific day and describes finished work.
quests.explanation: Finished is the simple past form, correctly used for completed work tied to a specific past day.

quests.sentence: By tomorrow's deadline, she'll have completed every section.
quests.hint: Tomorrow's deadline is the future point by which the whole task should be finished.
quests.explanation: Will have completed is the future perfect form, correctly describing a task expected to be finished by a future point.

quests.sentence: I've broken my arm twice, both times skiing.
quests.hint: This is about a count of experiences over a lifetime, without one specific defining time.
quests.explanation: Have broken is the present perfect form, correctly used to describe a repeated life experience.

quests.sentence: I broke my arm the second time on an icy patch near the lodge.
quests.hint: This zooms in on one specific occasion with concrete details.
quests.explanation: Broke is the simple past form, correctly used for one specific, detailed past event.

quests.sentence: By the time the ski season ends, the resort will have recorded a record number of injuries this year.
quests.hint: The end of the season is the future point by which this total will be reached.
quests.explanation: Will have recorded is the future perfect form, correctly describing a total expected to be complete by a future point.
